instructions: The night before, or the morning of: Move the phyllo from the freezer to the fridge so it thaws slowly.
Put the rice in a bowl, cover it with warm water, and let it soak for 10 minutes. Rinse it and drain it well. Meanwhile, dice both onions and mince the garlic.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the lamb and one of the diced onions and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking up the meat, until browned. Turn the heat to medium, add the garlic, and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in 1 tbsp of the seven-spice, 1 tsp of the salt and 1/2 tsp of the Aleppo pepper. Take it off the heat and cover it.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a small skillet over medium-low heat. Add the pine nuts and cook for 3 minutes, until golden. Transfer them to a plate.
Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the other diced onion and cook for 5 minutes, until soft but not browned.
Add the rice and cook for 1 minute. Add the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods and cloves and cook for 30 seconds, until they smell toasty.
Stir in the peas and carrots, the other 1 tbsp seven-spice, 1 1/4 tsp of the salt, the other 1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper and the turmeric. Pour in the broth, warmed, and stir once.
Bring to a gentle boil, then cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes without lifting the lid. Leave it covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.

Pick out the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods and cloves. Fluff the rice with a fork, then fold in the lamb and the pine nuts. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Let it cool for 10 minutes.
Melt the other 6 tbsp butter. Lay out 1 sheet of phyllo, brush it with butter, and layer 4 more on top, brushing each. Keep the rest of the phyllo under a damp towel.

Spoon a quarter of the filling into the middle of the stack. Fold the sides over the filling, then the ends, to make a closed square parcel. Flip it seam side down onto the baking sheet and brush the top with butter. Make 3 more the same way.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Chop 3 tbsp of the parsley and sprinkle it over the parcels. Serve with the yogurt.
To store, refrigerate in a covered container for up to 4 days, or freeze the unbaked filling for up to 3 months. Reheat the parcels on a baking sheet in a 350°F oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
advance_prep_notes: thaw the phyllo in the fridge overnight
method_notes: The lead (Falasteeni Foodie, 5.0 from 5) wraps spiced beef and rice with peas in buttered phyllo and bakes at 425°F. Its water amount is missing, so the rice-to-liquid ratio and the lamb, whole spices and nuts come from An Edible Mosaic's lamb ouzi (5.0 from 3). Phyllo is usually bought frozen and thawed overnight. Honest total is about 90 minutes, over 60, so it is a weekend family meal that keeps 3 to 4 days.
